entry.title: Using JooqTemplate implement UserService Demo
Why Plumeria?
entry.summary:
"CSS Modules are fine after all."
If you build web interfaces for a living, you have probably said this. After wrestling with runtime CSS-in-JS configuration, chasing specificity bugs across dynamic boundaries, or watching a utility-first framework bloat your markup, returning to the humble CSS Module feels like a relief. That isn't a compromise made for lack of features. CSS Modules win because they are predictable: the CSS you write behaves exactly as written. There is no runtime parser guessing your intent, no injection-order races between chunks, and almost no runtime JavaScript — just a class mapping object. But the safety has a price. You give up TypeScript-integrated styling, compile-time validation, dynamic theming, and seamless colocation. Plumeria is designed to eliminate this …

entry.summary: Introduction As software applications grow in size and complexity, managing object creation becomes challenging.
